title: Chat-to-Result capture
summary: Future explicit action such as `Add this to DashGPT` should distill the useful outcome of the current discussion into a reviewable Result and attach/update the appropriate Semantic Dash.
decisions: Do not assume every raw chat should be stored.
The user reviews what becomes a durable Result.
Capture should update the appropriate Dash without duplicating raw history.
next: Specify a separate OpenSpec change for current-chat capture, including review-before-save and Dash attachment/update semantics.

title: Storage: Local Vault
summary: Vault v1 provides the local-first portable storage core for Results, Dash revisions, assets/user state and append-only events, including migration and export/import.
decisions: The portable Vault is provider-neutral.
Core use remains local-first and cloud-optional.
Immutable Result knowledge stays separate from mutable user state.
next: Keep local Vault compatibility as new storage adapters and product-board metadata evolve.

title: Storage: GitHub adapter
summary: GitHub synchronization implements the Vault adapter boundary using the same provider-neutral objects instead of redefining DashGPT around GitHub.
decisions: GitHub is an adapter, not the domain model.
Credentials never enter the portable Vault.
Implementation merge and production activation are separate states.
next: Do not conflate merged adapter code with production activation; keep the activation smoke test on its own card.

title: Storage: Production GitHub activation
summary: Production GitHub sync still requires protected Worker configuration and one real private-repository end-to-end smoke test before the storage slice can be treated as activated.
decisions: Never paste or commit the GitHub App private key or session-signing secret.
A real repository smoke test is required before claiming production activation.
next: Configure the production Worker secrets outside chat/repository/Vault, then run pair → sync → idempotent re-sync → disconnect against a disposable private repository.

title: Storage: Google Drive
summary: Google Drive is a planned synchronization adapter that should reuse the same StorageLocator/Vault contract and explicit provider authorization.
decisions: Cloud synchronization is opt-in.
Provider authorization remains explicit.
Google Drive must reuse the same portable Vault model.
next: Create the dedicated storage slice/OpenSpec change and reuse the provider-neutral Vault contract rather than adding Drive-specific domain semantics.

title: Storage: Provider switching and mirroring
summary: Future storage UX should allow moving or mirroring the same portable Vault across supported providers without making any one provider authoritative.
decisions: Provider changes must not rewrite immutable Result knowledge.
Conflicts must be preserved rather than silently discarded.
The user owns and can export the Vault independently of a provider.
next: Specify conflict-preserving switch/mirror semantics after the next storage adapters use the same Vault contract.

title: Storage: Authenticated private Vault access
summary: Hosted ChatGPT/MCP access to a user's private paired Vault needs an authenticated storage/runtime boundary; current public MCP reads only intentionally exposed catalogs.
decisions: Public MCP access must not imply access to a private Vault.
Authentication is enforced before private content is delivered.
Provider credentials are never Result/Profile/Vault content.
next: Define and implement an authenticated private storage/runtime slice without weakening current public-catalog privacy boundaries.
